2609.14970.title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
2609.14970.paper_summary: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) increasingly rely on large-scale transcriptomic pretraining, yet expanding pretraining data can yield diminishing gains while substantially increasing computational cost. Our data scaling analyses showed that incorporating biological knowledge, including cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information, provided additional scaling dimension than simply increasing data size. Motivated by this observation, we present scKITE, a simple yet effective scFM that integrates cell-annotation and gene-regulatory supervision into a shared transcriptomic Transformer encoder through lightweight auxiliary decoders. These decoders are used only during pretraining and subsequently discarded, yielding a general-purpose encoder enriched with biological knowledge for downstream applications. With only 179,067 pretraining samples, i.e., less than 0.5\% of those used by previous strong scFMs, scKITE outperformed these models across diverse downstream tasks, highlighting knowledge-enhanced pretraining as a promising paradigm for biologically grounded scFMs.
2609.14970.paper_summary_zh: 單細胞基礎模型（scFMs）越來越依賴大規模的轉錄組預訓練，但擴展預訓練數據可能會帶來收益遞減，同時大幅增加計算成本。我們的數據擴展分析顯示，納入生物知識，包括細胞級文本註釋和基因級調控信息，提供了比單純增加數據量更額外的擴展維度。受到這一觀察的啟發，我們提出了scKITE，一個簡單但有效的scFM，通過輕量級輔助解碼器將細胞註釋和基因調控監督整合到共享的轉錄組Transformer編碼器中。這些解碼器僅在預訓練期間使用，隨後被丟棄，從而產生了一個富含生物知識的通用編碼器，適用於下游應用。僅用179,067個預訓練樣本，即少於之前強大scFMs使用的0.5\%，scKITE在各種下游任務中超越了這些模型，突顯了知識增強預訓練作為生物學基礎scFMs的一個有前途的範式。
